shows.bio: Founded in 1946 by Christian Dior; the 1947 “New Look” reshaped postwar fashion and still anchors the house's silhouette today. Jonathan Anderson became sole creative director in 2025, the first person to oversee womenswear, menswear, and couture together.

shows.playlist: Lady Gaga's “Just Dance” (remixed), with a Billy Elliot voiceover and a Pride & Prejudice score cue
shows.bio: French couture house founded in 1910 by Gabrielle “Coco” Chanel; built its identity on tweed suiting, the little black dress, and No. 5. Matthieu Blazy has been creative director since 2025, arriving from Bottega Veneta.
Founded in 1961 by Yves Saint Laurent and Pierre Bergé; credited with bringing the tuxedo (Le Smoking) into womenswear. Anthony Vaccarello has been creative director since 2016.

Founded in 2001 by Stella McCartney in London; the house has been leather- and fur-free from day one and has since developed plant-based faux fur and lab-grown vegan silk. McCartney remains creative director of her own label.

Spanish leather goods house dating to 1846 in Madrid, among the oldest names on any fashion week calendar. Jack McCollough and Lazaro Hernandez, the founders of Proenza Schouler, became co-creative directors in 2025.

Founded in 1952 by Hubert de Givenchy, closely associated with Audrey Hepburn's screen wardrobe in the 1950s and '60s. Sarah Burton has been creative director since 2024, following two decades at Alexander McQueen.
Founded in 1969 by Rei Kawakubo in Tokyo, long associated with deconstruction and challenging conventional ideas of beauty. Kawakubo remains creative director of her own label.

Founded in 2012 by Virgil Abloh in Milan, credited with helping bring streetwear into the luxury runway conversation. Abloh died in 2021; the brand has since been without a permanent creative director following Ib Kamara's departure.

shows.debut: Maria Grazia Chiuri's debut as creative director
shows.bio: Founded in 1925 by Adele and Edoardo Fendi in Rome, starting as a fur and leather workshop. Maria Grazia Chiuri became creative director in 2026, arriving from Dior.

shows.debut: Meryll Rogge's debut as creative director
shows.bio: Founded in 1994 by Consuelo Castiglioni in Milan, known for offbeat prints and asymmetric silhouettes. Meryll Rogge became creative director in 2026, following her own eponymous label.

shows.debut: Demna's runway debut as creative director
shows.stylist: Styled in-house by Demna — no separate stylist credited
shows.bio: Founded in 1921 by Guccio Gucci in Florence, originally producing leather luggage. Demna became creative director in 2025, arriving from Balenciaga.

shows.venue: A palazzo near La Scala, Milan
shows.bio: Founded in 1966 in Vicenza, Italy; best known for its intrecciato woven leather technique. Louise Trotter has been creative director since 2025, arriving from Carven.

shows.playlist: A 90s rave-leaning set — D-Shake, Dustin Zahn, and Robert Hood among the tracks, growing more erratic as the show went on
shows.bio: Founded in 1913 by Mario Prada in Milan as a leather goods shop; became a fashion house under Miuccia Prada from the 1980s on. Miuccia Prada and Raf Simons have served as co-creative directors since 2020.

shows.debut: Loris Messina and Simone Rizzo's debut as co-creative directors
shows.bio: Founded in 1983 by Franco Moschino in Milan, built on a tradition of pointed, satirical takes on fashion itself. Loris Messina and Simone Rizzo, formerly of Sunnei, were named co-creative directors in 2026.

Founded in 1913 by Mario Prada in Milan as a leather goods shop; became a fashion house under Miuccia Prada from the 1980s on. Miuccia Prada and Raf Simons have served as co-creative directors since 2020.
Founded in 1968 in Hamburg by Jil Sander, known for minimalist, clean tailoring; acquired by Prada in 1999 and later by OTB Group in 2021. Simone Bellotti has served as creative director.

shows.venue: Via Cola Di Rienzo angolo Via Moisè Loria, Milan

shows.bio: Founded in 1925 by Adele and Edoardo Fendi in Rome, starting as a fur and leather workshop. Maria Grazia Chiuri became creative director in 2026, arriving from Dior.

shows.venue: Via Dei Cavalieri Del Santo Sepolcro, Milan

shows.bio: Launched in 1997 as “Line 6” within Martin Margiela’s numbered house structure — a more casual, street-inspired counterpart to the main Maison Margiela line. True to Margiela’s ethos, MM6’s collections are directed by an anonymous studio collective rather than a named designer.

Founded in 1951 in Reggio Emilia by Achille Maramotti, still family-owned. Rather than a single creative director, design is led by a longtime studio team under design director Laura Lusuardi, with chairman Luigi Maramotti.
Founded in 1994 by Consuelo Castiglioni in Milan, known for offbeat prints and asymmetric silhouettes. Meryll Rogge became creative director in 2026, following her own eponymous label.
Italian label built around a romantic, rose-strewn femininity by Anna Molinari, nicknamed the “queen of roses.” A family business: her daughter Rossella also designs for the house.
Founded in 1921 by Guccio Gucci in Florence, originally producing leather luggage. Demna became creative director in 2025, arriving from Balenciaga.

Founded in 1927 by Salvatore Ferragamo, the shoemaker to Hollywood’s golden age. Maximilian Davis has been creative director since 2022, bringing a contemporary, playful edge while staying rooted in the house’s codes.

Founded in 1985 in Legnano by Domenico Dolce and Stefano Gabbana, epitomizing Italian glamour and sensuality. Gabbana stepped down as chairman in late 2025 but remains co-creative director alongside Dolce.
Founded in 1966 in Vicenza, Italy; best known for its intrecciato woven leather technique. Louise Trotter has been creative director since 2025, arriving from Carven.

Founded in 1975 by Giorgio Armani, who redefined masculine and feminine elegance through deconstructed, minimalist tailoring. Armani passed away in September 2025 at age 91; his niece Silvana Armani, already his longtime design deputy, now leads ready-to-wear.

Founded in 1856 by Thomas Burberry in Basingstoke, England; invented gabardine and popularized the trench coat. Daniel Lee has been creative director since 2022. ReBurberry Services offers repair, reproofing, and restoration for existing pieces.
Founded in 2005 by Erdem Moralioğlu in London, known for painterly florals and literary, historical references. Moralioğlu remains creative director of his own label.
Founded in 2010 by Simone Rocha in London, known for pairing romantic, feminine fabrics with harder, more confrontational details. Rocha remains creative director of her own label.
London-based designer known for “reformative luxury” built on deadstock fabric, upcycled denim, and leather. Coker remains creative director of her own label.

Founded by Emma Chopova and Laura Lowena in London, known for kilts and pieces built from recycled materials and deadstock textiles like pillowcases and aprons. Chopova and Lowena remain co-creative directors of their own label.
American designer based between London and New York, known for upcycling deadstock fabric and secondhand garments into new pieces. Ives remains creative director of his own label.
Founded in 2016 by Catherine Holstein in New York, known for elevated, quietly sexy basics. Holstein remains creative director of her own label.

shows.debut: Rachel Scott's debut with full creative control
shows.bio: Founded in 2002 by Jack McCollough and Lazaro Hernandez, then Parsons classmates, in New York. Rachel Scott became creative director in 2026 after the founders' move to Loewe.

shows.venue: Sotheby's (Marcel Breuer building), Madison Avenue, New York
shows.bio: Founded in 2004 by Tory Burch in New York, built around a preppy-with-an-edge American style. Burch remains creative director of her own label.

American leather goods house founded in 1941 in New York; Stuart Vevers has been creative director since 2013, leaning the house into youthful, downtown Americana. Its (Re)Loved program repairs, restores, and buys back used Coach pieces for resale.

Founded in 2011 by Mike Eckhaus and Zoe Latta in Los Angeles, now showing in New York; known for raw, unfinished-looking construction and a longstanding pre-loved runway partnership with eBay. Eckhaus and Latta remain co-creative directors of their own label.
American designer who launched his eponymous label in the 1980s; credited with bringing grunge to the runway in 1992. Jacobs remains creative director of his own label.
Founded by Elsa Schiaparelli in 1927, revived in 2012 and now led by Daniel Roseberry, known for surrealist, body-as-object couture. Traditionally opens the official Haute Couture calendar.

Founded by Christian Dior in 1946. Jonathan Anderson took over as creative director in 2026 following Maria Grazia Chiuri's departure to Fendi, his first couture-house role after Loewe and JW Anderson. In-store service desks offer repair and restoration for existing Dior pieces.

French couture house founded in 1910 by Gabrielle “Coco” Chanel; built its identity on tweed suiting, the little black dress, and No. 5. Matthieu Blazy has been creative director since 2025, arriving from Bottega Veneta.

Founded in 1919 by Cristóbal Balenciaga in San Sebastián before relocating to Paris; long regarded as a technician's house for its sculptural tailoring. Pierpaolo Piccioli became creative director in 2025, arriving from Valentino.

Founded by Jean Paul Gaultier in 1976. After years of rotating guest designers presenting couture under his name, Duran Lantink was named permanent creative director in 2026 to carry the house's sculptural, boundary-pushing legacy forward.
Giorgio Armani's couture line, launched in 2005. Following Giorgio Armani's death, Silvana Armani has led creative direction of the house.
Founded by Lebanese designer Elie Saab in 1982, a couture mainstay known for intricate embroidery and red-carpet eveningwear.
Dutch conceptual design duo Viktor Horsting and Rolf Snoeren, known for theatrical, art-driven couture presentations.

shows.debut: New couture house debut on the official Paris calendar
shows.bio: A newly launched couture house from Olivier Theyskens, debuting on the official Paris Haute Couture calendar.

Vivienne Westwood was founded in 1971 in London by Vivienne Westwood and Malcolm McLaren, emerging from their King's Road shop into a defining force in punk fashion. Its bridal line — Bridal Couture, Made to Order, and AK for VW — has been a cult favorite since Westwood's own SS1992 runway debut of bridalwear; the house staged its first-ever full bridal fashion show in 2025.
Israeli bridal house founded in 2004 by Berta Balilti, a Shenkar College graduate now based in Ashdod, Israel, known for bold, figure-hugging silhouettes and dramatic embellishment.

Founded in 1984 in Tel Aviv by Galia Lahav; in 2017 became the first Israeli brand accepted into the Chambre Syndicale de la Haute Couture and to present at Paris Fashion Week. Known for sheer overlays, corsetry, and romantic, couture-level craftsmanship.

Hayley Paige Gutman entered bridal design in 2011 at age 25, known for playful, whimsical gowns. After a multi-year legal dispute over rights to her own name, she relaunched independently under Hayley Paige in 2024; her REIN collection drew on equestrian tradition and Belle Époque ornamentation.

Israeli designer Pnina Tornai began making wedding dresses in 1992 and has partnered with New York's Kleinfeld Bridal — the salon behind TLC's Say Yes to the Dress — for two decades, known for her signature sexy, corset-driven silhouettes.

Founded in 1984 in Toronto by Ines Di Santo, an Italian-Argentine designer known for glamorous, art-influenced bridal and eveningwear couture. Her daughter Veronica joined the business in 1998 and now serves as managing partner.
Founded in 1986 in Dallas by Vatana Watters, known for sculptural silhouettes and handcrafted detail across its Watters, Wtoo, and Willowby collections.

Founded in 1985 by Amsale Aberra and Neil Brown after Aberra, an Ethiopian American designer, couldn't find a simply modern gown for her own wedding. Aberra became the first Black woman inducted into the CFDA; she died in 2018 and the house continues under her name, with a flagship in SoHo.

American leather goods house founded in 1941 in New York; Stuart Vevers has been creative director since 2013, leaning the house into youthful, downtown Americana. Its (Re)Loved program repairs, restores, and buys back used Coach pieces for resale.
Founded in 1967 by Ralph Lauren, built on an aspirational, preppy vision of American style — the polo player logo among the most recognized in fashion.
Founded in 2012 by Jasmin Larian in Los Angeles, best known for its bamboo Ark bag and resort-driven silhouettes.
Founded in 2001 by Rachel Comey in New York, known for architectural, artisanal womenswear with an unconventional edge; celebrated its 25th anniversary this season.
Founded in 2000 by Johnson Hartig in Los Angeles, known for whimsical, screen-printed, embellished pieces built from vintage and secondhand garments.

shows.debut: Henry Zankov's runway debut as artistic director
shows.venue: Under the High Line, New York
shows.bio: Founded in 1970 by Diane von Furstenberg, best known for inventing the wrap dress in 1974. Henry Zankov became artistic director in 2026, the brand's first appointment to that role.
Founded in 2016 by Emily Adams Bode Aujla in New York, built around vintage quilts, antique textiles, and other repurposed material. Bode Aujla remains creative director of her own label.

Founded in 2011 by Mike Eckhaus and Zoe Latta in Los Angeles, now showing in New York; known for raw, unfinished-looking construction and a longstanding pre-loved runway partnership with eBay. Eckhaus and Latta remain co-creative directors of their own label.
American designer based between London and New York, known for upcycling deadstock fabric and secondhand garments into new pieces. Ives remains creative director of his own label.
Founded in 2016 by Catherine Holstein in New York, known for elevated, quietly sexy basics. Holstein remains creative director of her own label.
Founded in 2002 by Jack McCollough and Lazaro Hernandez, then Parsons classmates, in New York. Rachel Scott became creative director in 2026 after the founders' move to Loewe.

shows.venue: Sotheby's (Marcel Breuer building), Madison Avenue, New York
shows.bio: Founded in 2004 by Tory Burch in New York, built around a preppy-with-an-edge American style. Burch remains creative director of her own label.
Founded in 2001 by Thom Browne in New York, built around a signature shrunken gray suit and reinventions of American tailoring. Browne remains creative director of his own label.
Founded in 1999 by Sabyasachi Mukherjee in Kolkata, known for opulent, heavily embroidered Indian bridal and couture work. Mukherjee remains creative director of his own label.
New York-based womenswear label founded by Trish Wescoat Pound, dedicated to reimagining the modern woman's closet.

Founded in 2021 by Terrence Zhou, a New York-based designer known for maximalist, fantastical silhouettes — balloon gowns, sculptural creature-inspired pieces — worn by Rina Sawayama and Christina Aguilera.
Founded in 1985 by Tommy Hilfiger, built around preppy American sportswear and the brand's signature flag logo.
Founded in 2002 by Stacey Bendet in New York, known for flirty, print-driven contemporary womenswear.
Founded in 2012 by South African-born designer Daniella Kallmeyer in New York, known for fluid, body-conscious tailoring.
Founded in 2013 by Rebecca Hessel Cohen in New York, known for romantic, ruffled florals and immersive, theatrical presentations.
Founded in 2008 by Christian Siriano, who won the fourth season of Project Runway that same year; known for red-carpet gowns in extended size ranges.
Founded in 2008 by Dao-Yi Chow and Maxwell Osborne in New York, known for elevating utilitarian streetwear into tailored ready-to-wear.

New York-based designer known for technology-enhanced shape engineering and fabric-first, sculptural experimentation over traditional themed collections. Named to the Forbes 30 Under 30 list in 2025; worn by Beyoncé and Katy Perry.
Founded in 1981 by Michael Kors in New York, built around jet-set American luxury sportswear.
Houston-born designer Amir Taghi (b. 1996) began designing as a teenager, interning with Oscar de la Renta before making his NYFW debut in 2014.
Founded in 1996 in New York, known for wearable, tailored contemporary womenswear rather than runway spectacle.
Founded by Jackson Wiederhoeft in New York, known for corsetry-driven, exaggerated eveningwear silhouettes.
One of New York's newer womenswear designers, known for a considered, unconventional approach to dressing.

Founded in 1968 by Calvin Klein, long defined by minimalist tailoring and its signature underwear and denim lines. Veronica Leoni became creative director in 2025, marking Calvin Klein Collection's return to the runway after a hiatus since 2018.
Founded by Christian Cowan, known for maximalist, sequined eveningwear with a camp sensibility.
Founded in 2015 by Laura Kim and Fernando Garcia, who are also co-creative directors of Oscar de la Renta.
Founded by Kim Shui, a Hong Kong-born, New York-based designer known for glossy, futuristic party clothes.
Founded in 2004 by Jonathan Simkhai in Los Angeles, known for body-conscious eveningwear and knitwear.
Rio Uribe founded Gypsy Sport in 2012 after working his way up to head of merchandising at Balenciaga, building a brand known for gender-fluid, inclusive casting and streetwear-luxury mixes.

Eritrean-born designer Nardos Imam launched her namesake luxury house in 2012 after training in costume design and working as in-house designer at Dallas' Stanley Korshak. Flagships in Dallas and on Madison Avenue, NYC.
Founded in 2008 by Joseph Altuzarra in New York, known for sensual, body-conscious tailoring.
Los Angeles-based label launched in 2022 by Kari Vettese, drawing on her Italian heritage; worn by Charli XCX, Florence Pugh, and Kylie Jenner.

shows.debut: Nicola Brognano's runway debut as creative director
shows.bio: Founded in 2000, one of the brands credited with launching the premium denim category. Nicola Brognano, formerly of Blumarine, became creative director in 2026.
Founded in 1981 by Anna Sui in New York, known for bohemian, vintage-referencing prints.
Founded in 1997 by Amy Smilovic, known for elevated, texture-driven contemporary basics.
Founded in 2009 by Prabal Gurung in New York, known for bold color and a strong focus on inclusivity in casting.
Founded in 2014 by Colm Dillane in New York, blending streetwear with theatrical, narrative-driven runway presentations.
Founded in 1998 in New York (originally as As Four), a design collective known for geometric, sculptural, and technology-driven garments.

Milwaukee-born, Puerto Rican-heritage designer Elena Velez (b. 1994) trained at Parsons and Central Saint Martins, known for synthesizing metalsmithing with high fashion. Named CFDA's 2022 Emerging Designer of the Year.
Denim-focused ready-to-wear label founded by Fforme co-founder Nina Khosla and Talia Shuvalov (ex-Alexander McQueen, Alexander Wang), with Joey Laurenti (ex-Sies Marjan, Opening Ceremony) as CEO.
Founded in 2013 by Piotrek Panszczyk and Beckett Fogg in New York, known for maximalist crystal embellishment.
New York-based designer known for romantic, body-focused ready-to-wear built from deadstock materials into sculptural, historically-informed silhouettes.
Launched in 2007 as a more considered, design-led sister brand to H&M.
Founded in 2014 by Sandy Liang in New York, known for girlish, nostalgic downtown style.
Founded in 2013 by Polish designer Magda Butrym, known for florals and body-conscious silhouettes.

Founded in 2017 by Patricio Campillo, a Mexico City-born designer known for rigorous tailoring referencing charro culture and ranch life, sourced from small artisan workshops in Mexico. LVMH Prize semi-finalist, 2024.
Founded in 2016 by Sergio Hudson in South Carolina, known for power tailoring popularized by Kamala Harris and Beyoncé.
Founded in 2015 by Brandon Maxwell, who first came up styling and designing for Lady Gaga.
Founded in 2011 by Todd Snyder, known for reworking classic American menswear.
New York-based designer known for liquid-metal, biomechanical sculptural pieces that blur fashion and body armor.
Founded by costume and fashion designer Zaldy Goco, known for his long-running collaboration with Lady Gaga.

Trinidad-born designer Aisling Camps trained as a mechanical engineer before studying at Columbia University and the Fashion Institute of Technology. Known for sculptural, architectural knitwear made from Italian-sourced yarns out of her Brooklyn studio.
Founded in 1998 by Ulla Johnson in New York, known for artisanal detailing and a bohemian sensibility.
Founded in 1967 by Norma Kamali, a pioneer of the sleeping-bag coat and the modern swimsuit-as-outerwear silhouette.

Luxury womenswear label co-founded in 2022 by Nina Khosla (product designer, also of Ossou) and Laura Vazquez (former EVP of Jil Sander Navy and Perry Ellis), built on a tech-inflected, slow-fashion, direct-to-consumer model. Creative direction has changed hands since launch.
Founded by Zane Li, a 2026 CFDA/Vogue Fashion Fund finalist.
Los Angeles-based footwear and accessories designer Jamie Haller, known for sculptural heels and a Montecito retail store.
Fine jewelry label founded by George Inaki Root, working primarily in freshwater pearls.
New York jewelry brand by Julia Ferentinos, known for sculptural, antiquity-inspired pieces and a 2026 CFDA/Vogue Fashion Fund finalist.
Emily Dawn Long is a rising independent fashion designer and the founder of her eponymous New York City-based label known for blending vintage nostalgia with artisanal craft.
New York label founded by Claire Sullivan, a Vaquera co-founder who went solo in 2022, known for playful, culturally referential eveningwear.
Founded in 2020 by Henry Zankov in New York, known for colorful, playful knitwear. Zankov also became Diane von Furstenberg's artistic director in 2026.

Founded in 2016 by China-born Parsons graduates Siying Qu and Haoran Li, a genderless New York label that treats each season like a newspaper dispatch, using collections to explore a social issue the duo is passionate about — from coral reef preservation to pharmaceutical corruption. A 2019 CFDA/Vogue Fashion Fund finalist.
Founded in 2021 by Rachel Scott, drawing on Jamaican craft techniques like crochet; Scott also became Proenza Schouler's creative director in 2026.
Founded in 2008 by Bibhu Mohapatra, known for intricately embroidered eveningwear.

shows.venue: David H. Koch Theater, New York
shows.bio: Founded in 1981 by Carolina Herrera, long associated with ladylike tailoring and dramatic white shirting.
Founded in 2016 by Raúl López in New York, known for reworking utilitarian and streetwear shapes into elevated pieces.
Founded in 2009 by LaQuan Smith in Queens, New York, known for body-conscious, sex-positive eveningwear.
Namesake label of Kozaburo Akasaka (b. 1984, Tokyo), who graduated from Central Saint Martins with a first-class degree in menswear.
Luxury womenswear label built around the idea of forgotten traditions, founded by Stephanie Suberville and her husband Jeffrey Axford.
Fashion and media brand founded in Sacramento in 2014 by Keith “Rooftop” Herron, who started the brand at age 14 selling handmade stickers.
Founded in 2010 by Hillary Taymour in New York, known for upcycled fabrics and maximalist prints layered with an environmental message.
Founded in 2021 by Andrew Kwon in New York, built around eveningwear and bridal, worn by Regina Hall, Lucy Liu, and Sophia Bush on red carpets.
Founded in 2016 by Stephanie Pollack in Los Angeles, known for elevated, deconstructed denim and basics.
American designer who launched his eponymous label in the 1980s; credited with bringing grunge to the runway in 1992. Jacobs remains creative director of his own label.

Founded in 1968 by Calvin Klein, long defined by minimalist tailoring and its signature underwear and jeans lines. Veronica Leoni became creative director of Calvin Klein Collection in 2025, continuing the house's exploration of American minimalism.
Founded by Frederick Anderson, known for bold color and print in eveningwear.

Founded in 1979 by Irish designer Paul Costelloe, who was personal designer to Diana, Princess of Wales, from 1983 until her death. Costelloe passed away in November 2025; his son William Costelloe has since taken over as creative director.
Founded by Georgian designer Lado Keburia, known for architectural minimalism, monochromatic palettes, and gender-fluid silhouettes.
Derbyshire-born designer who enrolled at Central Saint Martins in 2022 and has worked at both Vivienne Westwood and Mulberry, running his independent label from South London alongside his studies.
Founded by Demon Zhang, blending Eastern philosophical approaches with Western construction techniques through artistic prints and sophisticated silhouettes.
Canadian-born, London-based knitwear designer known for figure-hugging silhouettes and for pioneering size-inclusive runway casting in the late 2000s.
Founded in 2020 by Harris Reed in London, known for theatrical, gender-fluid silhouettes. Reed has also been creative director of Nina Ricci in Paris since 2022.

Now in its third year, eBay Endless Runway is the only pre-loved, shoppable show on the official London Fashion Week schedule, staged in partnership with the British Fashion Council. Every look is made entirely from pre-loved fashion and can be bought in real time via eBay Live during the show.

Founded in 2011 by married couple Ksenia and Anton Schnaider in Kyiv, known for reworked, upcycled, and patchwork denim — including their signature “demi-denim” culotte-jean hybrid, originally made from secondhand denim.
Swedish designer and recent Central Saint Martins MA graduate, a 2026 LVMH Prize finalist making her LFW runway debut as a BFC NEWGEN recipient this season.

Turkish-born, London-based designer who founded his label in 2002 after graduating from Central Saint Martins’ MA program, where Domenico Dolce and Stefano Gabbana purchased pieces from his graduate collection. Known for romantic, “dark romanticism” silhouettes.
Central Saint Martins graduate Susan Fang is known for hand-crafted glass-bead accessories and her signature “air-weaving” technique, lacing layered materials into 3-dimensional forms.

British designer born in Dubai (1988), graduated from the University of Westminster in 2012, and showed with the Fashion East incubator for three seasons before her solo LFW runway debut in September 2014. A repeat BFC NEWGEN recipient.

Beijing-raised, Central Saint Martins-trained (BA and MA) designer who co-founded his eponymous brand with Yibo Chen (Royal College of Art). Focused on gender-neutral fashion, innovative knitwear, and sustainable textile practices.

Not a single label but a nonprofit talent incubator founded by Lulu Kennedy in 2000, staging group runway shows for emerging London designers each season since 2003, with backing from Topshop and the Greater London Authority.

East London designer known for tailoring-driven collections and immersive, party-style show formats staged in nightclub and subculture-adjacent venues, often working with Savile Row-trained tailor Charlie Allen.
Founded by Natasha Zinko, a London-based, Odesa-born designer trained at Central Saint Martins. Works largely from deadstock fabric in a closed-loop production cycle.

Welsh designer who founded his namesake house in 2022, working entirely by hand with plant-based, recycled, organic, and repurposed materials and natural dyes (logwood, madder, turmeric, onion skins). A 2024 LVMH Prize finalist and Sarabande Foundation resident.

Founded by Talia Lipkin-Connor, a Central Saint Martins 2020 graduate, and named for her great uncle’s Liverpool boutique Lucinda Byre. East London-based, built on heritage, ritual, and longevity over output.
London-based designer from Liverpool, working with upcycled materials and circular design principles; founded London Fashion Week's first Swap Shop.
Founded in the 1980s by John Richmond after graduating Kingston University in 1982; co-founded the Richmond-Cornejo label with Maria Cornejo in 1984 before launching his own eponymous line.

Founded by Priya Ahluwalia in London, built on upcycled and recycled materials and drawing on her Nigerian, Indian, and British heritage. Ahluwalia won the Queen Elizabeth II Award for British Design in 2021.

Paris-born designer who studied at École Duperré before a Central Saint Martins MA, working for Simone Rocha, Rejina Pyo, and Alexander Wang before launching her own hand-knit-driven label in 2022. Winner of the ANDAM Special Prize 2026 and a 2024 LVMH Prize finalist.
Norwegian-born, London-based designer Eli Khzouz presents sustainable luxury built on organic materials and a zero-waste approach.
Founded in 2017 by Charlotte Knowles and Alexandre Arsenault in London, known for lingerie-inflected, technical, body-conscious womenswear.
Founded by Richard Quinn in London, known for lavish, floral-printed eveningwear and a monarchy-adjacent following (the Queen once attended his show).
London-based designer trained at Central Saint Martins, whose work explores traditional Asian ideals of feminine beauty through delicate, romantic silhouettes.

Founded by Emma Chopova and Laura Lowena in London, known for kilts and pieces built from recycled materials and deadstock textiles like pillowcases and aprons. Chopova and Lowena remain co-creative directors of their own label.
Founded in 2010 by Simone Rocha in London, known for pairing romantic, feminine fabrics with harder, more confrontational details. Rocha remains creative director of her own label.
Vancouver-born, Korean-Canadian designer trained at Central Saint Martins, with early experience under Alexander McQueen, John Galliano, and Zac Posen before launching her own London label.
Founded in 2005 by Erdem Moralioğlu in London, known for painterly florals and literary, historical references. Moralioğlu remains creative director of his own label.
Founded in 2014 by Foday Dumbuya, blending British tailoring with West African heritage and craftsmanship.
British leather goods house founded in 1971; Christopher Kane took over as creative director in 2026.

British-Cypriot designer Charlie Constantinou founded his label in 2022 after a Central Saint Martins MA, building modular, adaptable garments from deadstock fabrics and artisanal hand-dyeing. An LVMH Prize semi-finalist (2023) who has collaborated with 66°North and Demon Footwear.
Founded by Roksanda Ilincic in London, known for architectural color-blocked silhouettes.
Founded by Lee Alexander McQueen in 1992, known for its theatrical, precisely tailored, and often confrontational take on British fashion. Seán McGirr has been creative director since 2023.

London-based label founded in 2020 by multidisciplinary artist Ronan Mckenzie. The name draws from the Ghanaian Ewe word for ‘God hears me,’ with collections exploring tactility and structure alongside Mckenzie’s wider practice in scent, furniture, and performance.
Founded by Greek designer Dimitra Petsa, known for her signature “wet look” draping technique that gives garments the appearance of being freshly emerged from water.

Founded in 1856 by Thomas Burberry in Basingstoke, England; invented gabardine and popularized the trench coat. Daniel Lee has been creative director since 2022. ReBurberry Services offers repair, reproofing, and restoration for existing pieces.
Founded in 2006 by Stine Goya in Copenhagen, known for bold color and print in otherwise minimal Scandinavian silhouettes.
Founded in 2001 by Henrik Vibskov in Copenhagen, known for theatrical runway sets and sculptural, textile-driven menswear and womenswear.
Founded in 2003 by Malene Birger in Copenhagen, known for fluid, elevated ready-to-wear in muted tones.
Danish label founded by Naja Munthe, known for bohemian-tinged, texture-driven ready-to-wear.
Copenhagen label known for quiet, minimalist basics made with an emphasis on organic and traceable materials.

shows.debut: CPHFW International Guest Slot, supported by The Climate Pledge
shows.bio: Founded in 2010 by Hillary Taymour in New York, known for upcycled fabrics and maximalist prints layered with an environmental message.

Founded in 1919 by Cristóbal Balenciaga in San Sebastián before relocating to Paris; long regarded as a technician's house for its sculptural tailoring. Pierpaolo Piccioli became creative director in 2025, arriving from Valentino.
Launched in 1993 by Miuccia Prada as a younger, more experimental sister label to Prada. Miuccia Prada remains its creative director.
Founded in 1854 by Louis Vuitton as a Parisian trunk maker, long before it became a ready-to-wear house. Nicolas Ghesquière has led womenswear since 2013; Pharrell Williams leads menswear.
Founded in 2017 by Marine Serre in Paris; builds every collection from upcycled deadstock and surplus fabric rather than new material. Serre remains creative director of her own label.

Berlin-founded, Paris-showing label by Christa Bosch and Cosima Gadient, known for raw-edged tailoring and working pre-loved pieces into its runway shows. Bosch and Gadient remain co-creative directors of their own label.
Founded in 1999 by Chitose Abe in Tokyo, known for “splicing” two or more garments into one hybrid piece. Abe remains creative director of her own label.
Founded in 1993 by Jun Takahashi in Tokyo, rooted in the city's punk and subculture scene. Takahashi remains creative director of his own label.

Founded in 1983 by Franco Moschino in Milan, built on a tradition of pointed, satirical takes on fashion itself. Loris Messina and Simone Rizzo, formerly of Sunnei, were named co-creative directors in 2026.

Founded in 1978 by Gianni Versace in Milan, known for bold prints and body-conscious tailoring. Pieter Mulier was named creative director in 2026, arriving from Alaïa, after the brand's ownership passed to the Prada Group.
Founded in 1988 by Woo Youngmi in Seoul; one of the first Korean designers to build a presence on the Paris runway calendar. Woo remains creative director of her own label.
Paris-based label known for playful, sculptural takes on everyday dressing.
Founded in 2015 by Liushu Lei and Yutong Jiang in Shanghai, known for girlish silhouettes with an unexpected edge. Lei and Jiang remain co-creative directors of their own label.
Chinese designer and Central Saint Martins graduate known for bold prints that mix traditional Chinese motifs with streetwear shapes. Chen remains creative director of her own label.
Copenhagen label that began as a cashmere knitwear line around 2000 before growing into one of Scandinavia's best-known ready-to-wear names. Ditte Reffstrup has been creative director since 2009.
Founded in 2015 by Cecilie Bahnsen in Copenhagen, known for voluminous, sculptural dresses in technical fabrics. Bahnsen remains creative director of her own label.
Brazilian designer showing in São Paulo, working across resort and eveningwear.
Founded in 2011 by Adebayo Oke-Lawal in Lagos, known for gender-fluid menswear rooted in Nigerian identity and storytelling. Oke-Lawal remains creative director of his own label.
Founded in 1999 by Sabyasachi Mukherjee in Kolkata, known for opulent, heavily embroidered Indian bridal and couture work. Mukherjee remains creative director of his own label.
Founded in 2009 by Dion Lee, an Australian designer known for structural cutwork and engineered tailoring. Lee remains creative director of his own label.
Made-in-Los-Angeles vegan label founded by Rooney Mara, built entirely from animal-free materials. Mara remains creative director of her own label.
